subject: Post-demo priorities + proposed trial outline for HaloHealth
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@halohealth.com>, Priya Anand <priya.anand@halohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo priorities + proposed trial outline for HaloHealth

Hi Jordan / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed trial outline so we can align on scope and ownership before procurement. Attaching a short POC requirements workbook and a prioritized eval checklist.

TL;DR (ask): Please confirm success criteria priority (A/B/C), whether you can start ingestion of a 30-day sample dataset by Apr 19, and who on your side will be the trial owner for day-to-day coordination. If that looks good, we’ll lock dates and provide an initial capacity estimate.

What we heard (from demo):
- Goal: Reduce turnaround time for discharge summary generation and automate clinical-coding suggestions for billing teams.
- Success metrics: 95% template match for summaries OR 20% reduction in manual summarization hours; coding precision > 90% on top-3 suggestions.
- Data: Structured EHR + free-text notes (PHI). You want Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated — we flagged both options.

Proposed trial outline (high level):
1) Prep (1 week): secure brief (DPA + network details), sample dataset (30 days, de-id or secure transfer), test account access. Owner: HaloHealth trial lead.
2) Ingestion & baseline (1 week): Redwood loads sample, runs baseline metrics on current pipeline. Owner: Redwood (Ben) + HaloHealth eng.
3) Eval sprint (2 weeks): run inference runs, collect quality metrics against labeled subset, run latency/cost profiling. Success criteria gating (pass if >= threshold or show clear improvement path). Owner: Marissa (Redwood) + HaloHealth product.
4) Wrap & next steps (1 week): review results, propose production rollout or extended trial.

Owners suggested (Redwood):
- Trial PM: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.inference) — overall schedule and acceptance criteria
- Infra / capacity: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.inference) — dataset ingestion, sizing, and firewall/VPC checklist
- Technical lead (model & eval): Sofia Ivanova — evaluation plan, prompts, and quality gating

Attachments: halo_POC_requirements.xlsx (data fields + env checklist), redwood_prioritized_eval_checklist.pdf (success criteria + measurement), Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HaloHealthTrialShared

Next steps (proposed):
- Jordan/Priya: confirm trial owner + preferred start week (we suggested week of Apr 19) and mark top-2 success metrics as priority A/B.
- Redwood: follow with capacity estimate (Ben) and updated eval checklist by EOD Apr 6.

If you prefer, we can convert this outline into a mutual action plan (MAP) in HubSpot and route approvals there.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@halohealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Anand <priya.anand@halohealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo priorities + proposed trial outline for HaloHealth

Thanks, Sofia — good summary and appreciated the clear owners. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) Data scope: the 30-day sample — will that include PHI or will you need a de-identified subset? We can provide either but want to confirm requirements.
2) Can you share a ballpark of the infra/cost for the 2-week eval sprint (GPU hours, expected egress, etc.) — we need that for initial approval.
3) Timeline: Apr 19 works on our side if we get the DPA and a short network checklist by Apr 12. 

On success metrics: Jordan priority list: A) coding precision on top-3 suggestions, B) reduction in manual summarization time. We want concrete gating (numbers) in the checklist.

Appreciate the work — will loop in our eng lead once we confirm data approach.

On Tue, Apr 5, 2027 at 14:05, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Hi Jordan / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed trial outline so we can align on scope and ownership before procurement....

Jordan Lee
Head of Product Innovation | HaloHealth
jordan.lee@halohealth.com | +1 (617) 555-7890

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@halohealth.com>, Priya Anand <priya.anand@halohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo priorities + proposed trial outline for HaloHealth

Thanks for the quick response, Jordan — answers inline and updated attachments.

1) Data scope: We can accept either de‑identified or secure PHI transfer into a Private deployment (customer VPC). For a quick trial, a de-identified 30-day sample is simplest and removes extra legal steps. If you prefer Private VPC with PHI, Ben will coordinate network/KMS details.

2) Ballpark infra/cost (initial estimate):
- Baseline sizing: 1 x A100 equivalent for parallel processing of 50k tokens/day sample; 3–5 A100 hours/day during active runs.
- Estimated GPU hours for the 2-week eval sprint: ~70–100 GPU hours.
- Rough cost guidance (hosted trial pricing): $6k–$9k for the sprint (will refine once we know concurrency and exact token volumes).
(See attached capacity_estimate.xlsx for a quick breakdown.)

3) Timeline: We can aim to start Apr 19 provided DPA + network checklist are in place by Apr 12. I uploaded an updated checklist and a prioritized success-criteria sheet to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HaloHealthTrialShared (file: redwood_prioritized_eval_checklist.pdf).

Updated owners & next steps:
- HaloHealth trial lead: please confirm (Jordan or Priya).
- Redwood trial PM: Marissa Cole (will send MAP + weekly check-in invite after your confirmation).
- Infra lead: Ben Carter (will begin sizing & provide final estimate by Apr 12).

Acceptance gating (examples in attached checklist):
- Coding precision (top-3) >= 90% (Priority A)
- Summarization throughput: 20% reduction in average time for clinical summaries (Priority B)
- Latency: median inference latency per document < 700ms (Priority C)

If those look ok, I’ll convert the Drive doc to a HubSpot MAP and share the HubSpot link for sign-off.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0123

Looping in my sizing notes — attached is a brief capacity_estimate.xlsx. Quick note: if HaloHealth expects peak concurrent runs or a higher token volume (e.g., >200k tokens/day) we should size to 2x A100 and that shifts estimate up ~60%.

I’ll run a short network checklist with HaloHealth infra once they confirm trial owner and preferred start.
